failure_summary: The offered KB term immediate_threat (canonicalPhrase "threat to make four next move", derived from opponentPunishment.tag) is board-false for its own required cell c5r4 on the decision and afterBest boards: column 5 holds only 2 discs, so the next disc lands at c5r3 and c5r4 is a non-gravity-top major threat there (visualize_board.sh 315233253621552234626653641 lists "col5 row4 (X)" with no [GT]; only the afterPlayed board 3152332536215522346266536414 marks it "[GT]"), which contradicts the same prompt reading-key rule "never upgrade a non-gravity-top threat into a next move claim" — and 4 of 5 runs echoed the canonical phrase verbatim.
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; runs 2-4 are null for those axes (not scored, not passing). A5 and A7 graded on all 5 runs. A1/A2/A6 and G7a/G7b_offered copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_subset_2026-08-26T15-47-56Z_served_mechanical.json (all pass; all 5 keys present). A4 run 0 FAIL: served prose says "your opponent still has to answer the threat to make four next move at column 5, row 4" — ownership is flipped (opponentPunishment.owner=1, so c5r4 is the opponent’s own winning square and the PLAYER must answer it), and "next move" is false on the decision/afterBest boards where c5r4 is not gravity-top. A4 run 1 FAIL: "it keeps the pressure on your opponent’s next-move four at the square at column 5, row 4" — after the better move (column 2) c5r4 is still non-gravity-top on the afterBest board, so no four is available next move there. A3 pass on both scored runs: the named tactic (opponent major threat at c5r4 on the diagonal c7r2-c6r3-c5r4-c4r5) is real on all three boards and IS the decisive reason — playing column 5 fills c5r3 and makes c5r4 gravity-top (afterPlayed solver score for column 5 = +7, immediate opponent win), while column 2 leaves it unreachable. A5 pass 5/5: 2nd-person address, no field names or engine meta; boardState=mid-game so A5b does not apply; the raw cNrM tokens in `mechanism` are humanized to "column N, row M" in servedExplanation (guardDiagnostics: no failures, no strippedSpecs), so no coordinate-notation charge. A7 pass 5/5: each run names a cause (the opponent four-in-a-row line and the square completing it) with locatable referents — runs 2 and 4 use bare demonstratives ("that key square", "that square") but both are wrapped in an emitted [zone:c5r4], which A7b explicitly accepts; the mechanism is not a fork, so A7c is N/A. G4/G5 verified against render_decision.finalMovestring 3152332536215522346266536414, and every alias spec checked board-true on its truthBoard (opp majors c1r2, c1r4, c5r4, c5r5, c5r6 and their windows on decision; you-major c1r3 with window c1r3,c2r4,c3r5,c4r6 on afterBest). G6 pass: patternOnAfterBestBoard=true is correct — "major at c5r4 (opp)" is still present on the afterBest board, so L3 (denial / "coming no matter what you play") is the right route. G7 pass 5/5: annotationRepairs empty on every run; single-square phrases sit on [zone:c5r4] and line phrases on [zone:windows:c7r2,c6r3,c5r4,c4r5] — shapes match roles, nothing over-wrapped. UNSCORED OBSERVATIONS (sub-sampled axes; recorded, not charged): run 4 would fail G2(a) — "it keeps your reply from opening up your opponent’s next-move four" says the played move enabled the pattern, which the L3 guardrail explicitly forbids; run 3 would likely fail A4 — "it meets your opponent’s next-move four at column 5, row 4" claims column 2 blocks c5r4, which it does not. Run 2 is the only run that avoids the "next move" upgrade (it omits the [term:immediate_threat] tag), so the underlying propensity is 4/5; both A4-scored runs failed identically, hence intermittent=false. Discrepancy noted, not charged: render_decision.requiredSet lists 2 entries (opp-major-3, opp-major-line-3) while the assembled prompt requires 3 (adding better-col). No run emitted [zone:better-col], but per Step 0 render_decision is ground truth for the required set, and both of its entries were emitted by all 5 runs.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: zones.terms[slug=immediate_threat].canonicalPhrase ("threat to make four next move"), derived from opponentPunishment.tag=immediate_threat / register=immediate
counterexamples.evidence: c5r4 is NOT gravity-top on the decision or afterBest boards — column 5 has height 2, so the next disc lands at c5r3. visualize_board.sh 315233253621552234626653641 lists "col5 row4 (X)" without [GT], and the afterBest board 3152332536215522346266536411 still lists it without [GT]; only 3152332536215522346266536414 (afterPlayed) shows "col5 row4 (X+O) [GT]". The term is offered with no board qualifier, so runs 0/1/3/4 asserted an immediate four on a board where the opponent cannot play that square next move. The prompt’s own reading key forbids exactly this ("match the frame’s own grain, never upgrade a non-gravity-top threat into a next move claim") and the L3 frame text itself correctly hedged with "(not yet reachable — the column needs to fill first)", so the defect is the term offer, not the frame.
